p: The Zero Latency system has been rolled out in venues around the world, and part of its appeal is that the games are designed specifically for free-roam play rather than adapted from home consoles. That means the levels are built around moving as a group, with plenty of moments where you have to cover each other, split up or regroup quickly. Take a minute before you start to agree who's watching which direction, and you'll be surprised how much better your team performs.

Want to make it a proper occasion? Birmingham is one of the best cities in the country for a group weekend, with loads of options for food and nightlife after your session. Digbeth, the creative quarter just east of the centre, is packed with street food, independent bars and the old Custard Factory, now a hub for artists and makers. If you fancy a curry, Birmingham is famous as the home of the balti, and the Balti Triangle in Sparkbrook is the place to head for one.

For families and anyone with a day to spare, there's plenty more to see. Thinktank, Birmingham's science museum at Millennium Point, is packed with hands-on exhibits, a planetarium and huge historic machines. Cadbury World in Bournville is a must for chocolate lovers, telling the story of the famous brand with plenty of tasty samples along the way.

The Jewellery Quarter, a short walk from the centre, is home to hundreds of jewellery businesses and some fascinating museums, including the Museum of the Jewellery Quarter, where a workshop has been preserved just as it was left. The Library of Birmingham in Centenary Square is worth a look too, with its striking design and rooftop gardens offering great views over the city. Birmingham New Street station is right in the city centre, making it easy to reach from across the country.
